failure_patterns.pattern: cached_followup_scope_or_omission: Follow-ups skipped requested updates or repeated filters for cached domains whose criteria had not changed.

rejected_edits.content: If the user explicitly replaces a category or entity criterion, treat the new value as superseding the conflicting old one rather than adding another filter. Do not filter results already restricted by the superseded value; retrieve the latest compatible result that is not so restricted, apply the new criterion while retaining still-applicable explicit criteria, and save it. If no compatible cached result exists, search anew for the replacement with those still-applicable criteria.
rejected_edits.target: If the user adds criteria, retrieve the closest compatible result, apply the matching filter, and save the updated result.

rejected_edits.content: Resolve explicit place references such as “there,” “that city,” or “the destination” to their unambiguous location antecedent in the conversation, including a stated trip destination, and use it in the matching domain field rather than asking again; if the antecedent is genuinely ambiguous, ask only for the missing location. When restaurants are explicitly requested alongside lodging in a named destination and no separate restaurant city is given, use the lodging destination city for the restaurant search. Run that restaurant search when its city is known even if hotel dates are missing, and seek only the missing hotel inputs.
rejected_edits.target: Still perform every independent requested search or update whose own required inputs are complete in the same turn.
